name: Reliable Event Pipeline → Slack (idempotent, with DLQ and canary)

parameters.content:
## Two ways in

The webhook is the production intake. The demo trigger exists so the whole thing can be run and filmed without wiring up a live CRM.

Both feed the same normalisation step, so what you see in the demo is what runs in production.

## Idempotency — the part buyers screen for

Events get replayed. Upstream systems retry. Without a gate here, one deal change becomes four Slack messages and the client turns the integration off.

The fingerprint hashes the event's *content*, not just its id, because some systems reuse ids and some omit them entirely.

The seen-set is TTL'd and capped — an unbounded one is a memory leak that surfaces in month four.

## Dead letter queue

When delivery fails after three retries, the event is captured with its full payload and the error — replayable once the downstream system is fixed.

It also **releases the fingerprint**, so the replay is not swallowed as a duplicate. That interaction between the two mechanisms is easy to get wrong and expensive to discover late.

## Canary — catching silence

The failure that costs real money is not a loud error. It is a webhook that quietly stops firing while everyone assumes it is working.

This runs daily and reports if nothing has been delivered in 26 hours, along with the current dead-letter depth.
